messages:
sara_dev: Heads up — onboarding sample app is hitting a weird hang in generator streaming. When token refresh retries occur we see handshake timeouts and what looks like goroutine leaks. Repro steps in sample-app v0.3.

mike_infra: Can you paste the failing logs or a minimal repro?

sara_dev: Log excerpt: `rpc: handshake timeout after 10s` repeated, then CPU climbs. Happens when auth server responds 401 -> we retry in SDK.

jamal_sdk: This smells like context cancellation not being wired into the transport/handshake flow. If retry creates a new request without cancelling the old stream, the runtime keeps the KV cache and goroutine around.

anna_docs: @sara_dev customer POC is blocked by this — any temporary config we can suggest?

sara_dev: Temporary: set `ClientOptions{AutoRetry:false}` and handle token refresh+reconnect in app code. Ugly but works. Also lowering handshake timeout to 3s makes the issue show up faster for debugging.

ollie_oncall: Minimal repro I used locally:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
defer cancel()
cli := inference.NewClient(token)
req := &inference.StreamRequest{Model:"gpt-small", Input:"loop"}
// Simulate auth flakiness by having token refresher sleep 5s before returning new token
stream, err := cli.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for tok := range stream.Recv() { fmt.Println(tok) }
```
When token refresh triggers inside SDK, old stream handshake goroutine never sees ctx.Done() and keeps waiting on net.Conn.

jamal_sdk: Thanks — I can reproduce. Suggestion: we should propagate the original ctx into the transport Dial/Handshake and ensure any retry path cancels previous handshake ctx before starting a new one. Also need an ergonomic hook for callers to explicitly cancel the generator stream without closing shared client.

sara_dev: API proposal sketch: introduce `StreamController` returned from Stream() with methods: `Recv()`, `Close()`, `CloseWithErr(error)`, and `Context()`. That lets the SDK take an owned ctx for each handshake and callers can call `CloseWithErr(context.Canceled)` to short-circuit.

anna_docs: Would that break existing sample apps? We should add a small migration doc and update quickstart snippet.

mike_infra: Also watch auth/retry interactions: if retry triggers a fresh token then handshake should restart but previous handshake must be cancelled immediately. We might add an internal backpressure channel so only one active handshake goroutine per stream id exists.

jamal_sdk: Implementation note: use `handshakeCtx, handshakeCancel := context.WithCancel(parentCtx)` per attempt. Store cancel in a small atomic so retry path can call it. For safety, make `StreamController.Close()` call cancel for whichever attempt is active.

sara_dev: I'll open a small PR with tests and an updated sample-app demonstrating correct cancellation and no leak. I'll include a migration snippet for docs.

ci-bot: CI: sample-app integration tests flaky: two failures in `stream_cancel_test` in last 12 runs.

ollie_oncall: @jamal_sdk @sara_dev if you need increased timeout on CI while you iterate, I can bump.
